title: Levy to fund dedicated Washington County Law Enforcement Services
ballot_label: Caption: Levy to fund dedicated Washington County Law Enforcement Services. Question: Shall City levy $2.50 per assessed $1,000 for five years beginning FY 2027-2028 for law enforcement services? This measure renews current local option taxes.
summary: The Banks city council referred a five-year local option levy of $2.50 per $1,000 of assessed value, beginning in 2027, to renew the levy in place since 2022. Funds would continue the city's contract with the Washington County Sheriff for full-time local police service: two deputies working a combined 80 hours a week. The city says the current contract expires June 30, 2027.
yes_means: A yes vote approves a five-year Banks local option levy of $2.50 per $1,000 of assessed value, beginning in 2027-28, to fund law enforcement services from the Washington County Sheriff.
no_means: A no vote rejects the levy; the city's explanatory statement says Banks would then have emergency-call response only, from an officer shared across west Washington County, after the current contract ends June 30, 2027.
fiscal_impact: Per the ballot title: $2.50 per $1,000 of assessed value for five years, about $250 a year on a $100,000 assessed home and $375 on a $150,000 home (estimates only). The levy would first appear on the property tax bill due November 2027. The ballot title states no total revenue figure.
